name: Gohma
arena: The basement of the Great Deku Tree
weak: Her eye, when it turns red
steps: Lock on to Gohma with ZL and wait for her eye to turn red.
Hit the eye with the Fairy Slingshot (or throw a Deku Nut up close) to knock her down.
While she is stunned on the floor, run in and slash the eye with the Kokiri Sword.
When she climbs to the ceiling she drops eggs: break them before Gohma Larvae hatch.
In the remake she shields her eye with her front legs while she is immune: save your seeds until she uncovers it.
reward: Heart Container. Afterwards, the Great Deku Tree gives you the Kokiri Emerald.
note: The remake calls her just "Gohma" (was "Queen Gohma"). You can rematch her in the Hall of Fallen Foes.

name: King Dodongo
weak: His open mouth, when he breathes in to spit fire
steps: When he opens his mouth and starts to inhale, throw a bomb into it.
Once he swallows it he is stunned: run in and hit him with your sword as much as you can.
Then he curls up and rolls around the room: step aside and wait for him to stop.
Avoid the lava at the edges and his fire breath; repeat until he goes down.
reward: Heart Container. On the way out, Darunia gives you the Goron Ruby.
note: Base-game strategy: the remake keeps the bosses but tweaks some patterns and adds rare new attacks (not yet confirmed for the remake). You can rematch it in the Hall of Fallen Foes. His statue recommends bombs.

name: Barinade
arena: The deepest part of Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly
weak: Its body, while it is stunned
steps: Throw the Boomerang at the tentacles that hold it to the ceiling (lock on with ZL) until they are all cut.
Once free it spins inside a ring of Biri: hit its body with the Boomerang to stun it.
Clear the Biri that break away and slash the body while it is stunned.
At the end it chases you and fires beams: keep your distance, stun it again with the Boomerang and hit it until it falls.
reward: Heart Container. Afterwards, Princess Ruto gives you the Zora Sapphire.
note: Base-game strategy: the remake keeps the bosses but tweaks some patterns and adds rare new attacks (not yet confirmed for the remake). You can rematch it in the Hall of Fallen Foes.

name: Phantom Ganon
weak: Phase 1: the real rider as he leaves the painting. Phase 2: his own energy balls.
steps: Phase 1: he rides between the paintings in the room. The fake turns back before coming out; the real one rides out of the painting at you: shoot him with the Fairy Bow.
After a few hits he comes down to fight: bat his energy balls back with your sword until one hits him.
When he drops stunned, run in and slash him. If he calls lightning from above, move away.
Keep up the rally until he is beaten.
reward: Heart Container. Saria awakens as a Sage and gives you the Forest Medallion.
note: Base-game strategy: the remake keeps the bosses but tweaks some patterns and adds rare new attacks (not yet confirmed for the remake). You can rematch it in the Hall of Fallen Foes. One source says his projectiles are slower in the remake.

name: Volvagia
arena: The top of the Fire Temple, above the lava
weak: Its head, when it pops out of a lava hole
steps: Wear the Goron Tunic: the remake has no heat timer, but without it you lose health fast.
Volvagia sticks its head out of one of the lava holes: run over and hit it with the Megaton Hammer before it dives back in.
While it is stunned, finish with your sword.
When it flies around the room, dodge its fire breath and the rocks that fall from the ceiling; arrows hurt it in the air.
Its statue in the Hall of Fallen Foes says that freezing its mouth stops its fire breath: try Ice Arrows (not yet confirmed for the remake).
reward: Heart Container. Darunia awakens as a Sage and gives you the Fire Medallion.
note: Base-game strategy: the remake keeps the bosses but tweaks some patterns and adds rare new attacks (not yet confirmed for the remake). You can rematch it in the Hall of Fallen Foes.

name: Morpha
weak: The nucleus, the ball that moves through the water
steps: Wear the Zora Tunic and stay on the platforms at the edges, away from the tentacles.
When the nucleus rises inside a tentacle, grab it with the Longshot to pull it out of the water.
Out of the water, slash it before it gets back in.
If a tentacle grabs you, move away as soon as it lets go; do not stand between two tentacles.
Its statue in the Hall of Fallen Foes says its tentacles are weak to heat (Din's Fire or Fire Arrows).
reward: Heart Container. Ruto awakens as a Sage and gives you the Water Medallion; in the remake Zora Domain also thaws.
note: Base-game strategy: the remake keeps the bosses but tweaks some patterns and adds rare new attacks (not yet confirmed for the remake). You can rematch it in the Hall of Fallen Foes.

name: Bongo Bongo
arena: The great drum at the bottom of the Shadow Temple
weak: The eye on its body, invisible without the Lenses of Truth
steps: Wear the Lenses of Truth (D-pad ↑) to see its body; they drain magic while worn.
Shoot an arrow (or the Hookshot) at each hand to stun it; the Hover Boots stop the drum from bouncing you.
With both hands stunned, shoot the eye on its body: it falls onto the drum.
Run in and slash it while it is down; repeat.
According to its statue in the Hall of Fallen Foes, freezing its hands stops it drumming (Ice Arrows).
reward: Heart Container. Impa awakens as a Sage and gives you the Shadow Medallion.
note: Base-game strategy: the remake keeps the bosses but tweaks some patterns and adds rare new attacks (not yet confirmed for the remake). You can rematch it in the Hall of Fallen Foes.

name: Twinrova
arena: The top of the Spirit Temple
weak: Phase 1: the other sister's spell. Phase 2: the energy stored in the Mirror Shield.
steps: Phase 1: Koume (fire) and Kotake (ice) attack separately. Catch one sister's beam with the Mirror Shield and aim it at the other: fire hurts Kotake and ice hurts Koume.
Phase 2: they merge into Twinrova. Absorb three blasts of the same element in a row with the Mirror Shield to charge it.
Release the charge at Twinrova; when she falls, slash her.
A blast of the other element wipes the charge: dodge it instead of blocking.
reward: Heart Container. Nabooru awakens as a Sage and gives you the Spirit Medallion.
note: Base-game strategy: the remake keeps the bosses but tweaks some patterns and adds rare new attacks (not yet confirmed for the remake). You can rematch it in the Hall of Fallen Foes. One source says her attacks were toned down in the remake.

name: Ganondorf
arena: The top of the tower of Ganondorf's Castle
weak: Light Arrows and his own energy spheres
steps: Bat his energy spheres back with your sword until one hits him, or shoot him with a Light Arrow while he floats.
When he drops stunned, jump to his platform and slash him.
If he breaks the floor, stay on the tiles that are left; when he charges the big sphere, shoot him with a Light Arrow.
Repeat until he falls: the castle starts to collapse.
note: Base-game strategy: the remake keeps the bosses but tweaks some patterns and adds rare new attacks (not yet confirmed for the remake). You can rematch it in the Hall of Fallen Foes. Save to a spare slot before you go up: the remake has no New Game+. The castle escape no longer has a timer.

name: Ganon
arena: The ruins of Ganondorf's Castle, inside a ring of fire
steps: At the start Ganon knocks the Master Sword away: fight with the Biggoron Sword or the Megaton Hammer.
Shoot Light Arrows at his face to stun him.
Roll between his legs or circle round him and hit his tail while he is stunned.
After enough hits he collapses: pick up the Master Sword, Zelda holds him in place and you strike the final blow.
note: Base-game strategy: the remake keeps the bosses but tweaks some patterns and adds rare new attacks (not yet confirmed for the remake). You can rematch it in the Hall of Fallen Foes.
